newsitem.title: canada: Canada pushes for early NATO deal with Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Canada pushes for early NATO deal with Ukraine.

text.p: Canada is pressing for a speedy conclusion to NATO agreements with Ukraine and Russia as the alliance plans its eastward expansion, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Wednesday.
Axworthy, speaking beside Ukrainian Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko, said the idea was to conclude the two agreements by the time of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation summit in Madrid in July.
The summit is expected to invite ex-communist Eastern European states like Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to join the group, formerly directed against the Soviet Union.
"I think it's very important that we get the agreements with Russia, with Ukraine concluded by the Madrid agreeement so it can all come together as a package," Axworthy told reporters.

Udovenko said negotiations on a special partnership agreement between Ukraine and NATO were a top priority during his visit to Canada as well as planned talks with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.
Since Ukraine does not oppose NATO's expansion plans, its agreement was likely to be easier to conclude than the one with Russia, which strongly opposes the NATO move.
Udovenko said the agreement would entail political consultations on a number of security issues, as well as political and economic cooperation.
Earlier on Wednesday Udovenko told the National Press Club in Ottawa that Russia must fully come to terms with the fact that Ukraine is independent.
"They need to change their mentality and understand that Ukraine is an independent country," he said, adding that it could take years to change the Russian mindset.
Ukraine became independent in 1991 and has struck a foreign policy line distinct from Russia's.
The minister -- who will also visit central Canada, home to numerous Ukrainian immigrants -- invited foreign investment.
He said Ukraine could absorb $30 billion to $40 billion in foreign investment to restructure industry. Since independence, Ukraine has attracted only $1.4 billion in private foreign investment.
